text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) and the government on Wednesday launched urgent talks to try and end a three week strike by junior doctors and nurses which has crippled the country's health system.

- A top Trans-Zambezi Industries executive says the ability of Zimbabwean companies to raise private capital on the international market should improve markedly when the regional conglomerate is listed on the London Stock Exchange next January.

- The Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA), still recovering from the recent shock of a controversial sale by government of its Hwange Thermal Power Station to YTL Corporation of Malaysia, has appointed an international law firm to give it legal and financial advice on the Z$6 billion deal, sources said.
- The Canadian Association for the Private Sector in Southern Africa project, which facilitated multi-million dollar investments by Canadians in Zimbabwe and the region, has been closed.
- A new Z$100 million venture capital company will be launched in Harare on Thursday to provide risk capital to companies in all sectors of the Zimbabwean economy.

- Zimbabwe's minister of state responsible for parastatals, Cephas Msipha, says the government has rescued at least 12 companies whose assets had been attached by financial institutions owing to mounting uncleared debts and other viability problems.

- Zimbabwe's health minister on Wednesday night released the full salary schedules of junior doctors and nurses in order to dispel what it believed to be attempts to mislead the public on the salary packages received by the medical workers.

- The first phase of a Z$1.5 million borehole drilling project undertaken by the Zimbabwe Tobacco Association to solve small-scale growers' water problems has now been completed and the second phase is expected to begin early next year.
